findings.evidence: ZkWhirOracleCommitter::commit_initial and initialize_sumcheck receive a host slice; HidingWhirProverData owns a host Poly. C62GpuWhirCommitter uploads that initial message. It has no borrowed resident-message entry for C6.3 D22/D19 limbs.

C63GpuStateOwner owns correction_rows, S and A on device, but the backend has no operation that projects their sixteen base-field columns by post-root rho into the two D22/D19 limb messages while preserving virtual-zero geometry.

C63ProjectedMmcs delegates to the CPU C61Mmcs and attaches CPU C63AProverData. C63GpuStateOwner exposes its A tree but no pruned resident row-opening method, so A-to-y cannot use the accepted device owner.

The joint four-lane construction, transcript replay and terminal closure are confined to the cfg(test) scaled reference. The production codecs exist, but there is no normal-path coordinator that creates the four proofs, sparse closure and designated tail from one response state.

C63NativeFinalCertificate::validate checks canonical framing, caps and digest/state consistency. It does not verify the four WHIR proofs, correction openings, sparse-H relation, output link, terminal authentication or inherited response proof in one call.

required_unblock: Add one exact resident sixteen-column projection operation with a CPU/GPU differential for compact D22 rows, column-major D19 S and virtual zeros.
Add a borrowed resident initial-message handoff to the existing WHIR prover without a witness-sized host Poly or a second encoding.
Open accepted A rows from C63GpuStateOwner into the existing canonical pruned proof and wrap C62GpuMmcs for the projected first round.
Promote the scaled four-lane transcript/replay logic into one production coordinator and one complete four-thread CPU verifier.
Pass mutation, cleanup, dense-path sentinel and resource-supervisor checks before any cold or warm E2E attempt.
